t: Founded by Sargon of Akkad, it is widely regarded as the world's first empire, uniting the Sumerian city-states under one ruler.
Its governors, standard measures and written Akkadian set the template that later Mesopotamian empires followed.
Gutian raids, palace murders and a severe drought around 2200 BCE brought it down; its capital has never been found.
dyk: Sargon's daughter Enheduanna, high priestess of the moon god at Ur, is often described as the first named author in recorded history.
ev: Sargon of Akkad founds the empire after supplanting King Ur-Zababa of Kish
Naram-Sin, Sargon's grandson, begins the reign that marks the empire's zenith
Akkadian power peaks under Naram-Sin, self-styled King of the Four Quarters
The 4.2-kiloyear drought brings crop failure and famine across the Near East
Shar-Kali-Sharri dies, leaving a chaotic succession of short-lived kings
The Akkadian dynasty comes to an end
